ideas.pitch: A 2D puzzle platformer where the environment changes its art style and physics retroactively based on the player recording and looping actions.
ideas.title: ChronoCanvas
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the nostalgia factor seen in retro gaming hackathon winners while fitting neatly into a 9-day game jam development window with tight mechanical scope.

ideas.pitch: A narrative-driven visual novel featuring branching dialogues where player choices simulate real-world resource allocation problems.
ideas.title: Echoes of Concetto
ideas.why_it_could_win: Follows the exact design pattern of educational narrative games that score high in public presentation formats like Concetto's 3-minute pitch.

ideas.pitch: A dungeon crawler where combat commands and spellcasting are executed by typing dynamic natural language prompts interpreted by a lightweight local LLM.
ideas.title: PromptQuest 2D
ideas.why_it_could_win: Brings the live-interaction agent element of winning AI hackathons into a structured indie game format that wows judges during the offline presentation.

ideas.pitch: A minimalist top-down action RPG featuring dynamically generated dungeon layouts and enemy behaviors to maximize replayability within jam limits.
ideas.title: Aethelgard: Procedural Legends
ideas.why_it_could_win: Focuses on clean, polished combat loops rather than overscoped content, which is the winning formula for standard indie game jams.

ideas.pitch: A physics-based arcade puzzle game where player progression unlocks simulated in-game micro-economy upgrades and node transactions.
ideas.title: TokenTether
ideas.why_it_could_win: Combines addictive arcade mechanics with gamified transactional loops that appeal to judges looking for functional, complete gameplay loops.
